items.title: SoftBank CFO Says “There Is No Such Default” After Musk’s Turbine Claim, But a $3.7B Charge on Scrapped Turbine Orders Suggests Elon Was Onto Something
items.summary: SoftBank's CFO called Elon Musk's turbine-default claim "simply not correct at all," and in the same results SoftBank wrote off about $3.7 billion of turbine equipment it will not take, most of it prepaid fees it cannot recover. Here is what the charge is, why GE Vernova says it felt nothing, and what it means for a retiree holding 100 spin-off shares.
